title: Dropbox / Google Drive
summary: Sync large files across devices using content-addressed chunks, consistent metadata and change notifications.
narrative:
A user edits a file on a laptop and expects the change to appear on a phone without uploading the entire file again. Build Dropbox / Google Drive with folders, sharing, upload/download of files up to 50 GB and cross-device sync. Split files into ~4 MB chunks addressed by content hash: a 50 GB file contains roughly 12,500 chunks using decimal units. Hashes enable deduplication, resumable uploads and delta sync of changed chunks.

Store the folder tree using parent_id, file-to-ordered-chunk mappings, sharing permissions and version metadata in a strongly consistent SQL Database sharded by user or namespace. Keep chunk bytes in Blob Storage replicated across regions. Web Servers authorize access, issue presigned chunk upload URLs and commit a new version only after required chunks exist; file bytes bypass the app servers. The Web Server → Blob Storage edge represents signing and commit checks, while clients can upload directly to storage and download through the CDN.

A Load Balancer distributes API requests across redundant Web Servers, which use replicated SQL metadata. Use conditional version commits to detect concurrent edits and preserve a conflict copy rather than silently losing an update; readers see a committed version and can retry a lagging regional blob replica. Publish committed file changes through Pub/Sub to WebSocket Servers, reached by devices through the Load Balancer. Push is a notification to fetch authoritative changes, with version cursors for reconnect catch-up. An optional metadata Cache must respect versions and permissions; Monitoring can expose replication and sync lag.

functional: Upload and download files up to 50 GB; support folders, sharing and cross-device sync
Split files into ~4 MB content-hashed chunks for deduplication, resume and delta sync
Store parent_id folder trees, ordered chunk lists, versions and sharing permissions in SQL; keep chunk bytes in Blob Storage
Authorize and sign direct chunk uploads in the app; commit metadata after chunk availability checks
Publish committed changes through Pub/Sub and WebSockets; reconcile missed changes using version cursors
nonFunctional: Keep metadata strongly consistent within a namespace and detect concurrent edits
Replicate chunks across regions and tolerate metadata replica failure
Transfer file bytes independently of app-server capacity
constraints: Client metadata access must pass through Web Servers; route the device sync channel through the Load Balancer
Allow presigned Client → Blob Storage uploads; use the CDN for downloads
Commit complete versions atomically and enforce sharing permissions before issuing storage access
Replicate SQL metadata with coordinated leadership; readers must handle lagging regional chunk replicas
capacity: Maximum file size: 50 GB; chunk size: ~4 MB
A 50 GB file has roughly 12,500 chunks with decimal units; delta sync transfers changed chunks only
Shard metadata by user/namespace; replicate chunk storage across regions
specs.tradeoff: Content hashing saves storage and bandwidth but requires chunk manifests and safe garbage collection. Strong metadata consistency simplifies version commits, while asynchronous regional blob replication requires lag-aware reads. Deduplication must not expose another user's private content.
specs.bonus: Connect Web Servers to a metadata Cache with version-aware invalidation and add Monitoring for sync and replication failures.

topologyRules.message: Clients must never access file metadata directly in SQL.
File metadata access must pass through the Web Server tier.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so metadata and upload authorization survive an instance failure.
Replicate SQL metadata across at least two database instances for failover.
Connect Blob Storage to a CDN for efficient chunk downloads.

hints: Separate file bytes from metadata: connect Client → Load Balancer → Web Server → SQL, and Client → CDN → Blob Storage for downloads. Store folder parents, ordered chunk hashes and versions in SQL.

Connect Web Server → Blob Storage for presigned upload authorization and commit checks; file bytes can upload directly to storage. Publish Web Server → Pub/Sub → WebSocket Server and connect Load Balancer → WebSocket Server for device sync.

Run two Web Servers and two SQL replicas, connecting each app replica to both database instances, Blob Storage and Pub/Sub. Add Web Server → Cache and → Monitoring; use version checks to invalidate metadata and resolve concurrent edits.
